requirements.requirement: Run a containerized web application as the unprivileged account appsvc on node1
requirements.summary: cmd-bc983cbcd21c4a29 shows appsvc user created, rootless podman container 'webapp' running under systemd --user unit owned by appsvc (uid 1000), confirmed via podman ps output showing the container process tree under user.slice/user-1000.slice.

cmd-bc983cbcd21c4a29 shows podman ps with 0.0.0.0:8080->8080/tcp and curl HTTP_CODE:200; independently confirmed by the after_executor lifecycle snapshot listening-sockets observation showing tcp LISTEN *:8080 owned by pasta (rootless podman network helper).

requirements.requirement: Application starts at boot while appsvc has no active login session
requirements.summary: Full bounded reboot transition was captured: pre-restart healthy baseline with boot_id f455a75c and active service/container/HTTP 200 (cmd-ceb4d139a0e947e3), a reboot acknowledgement returned before disconnection (cmd-46defdcad6c24dec), observed disruption via connection-reset polling (cmd-2f3421fb76744153, cmd-e9ad9dd851a84a18), reconnection with a new boot_id e0bd15c4 and reset uptime (cmd-805a85485b144700), and post-restart recovery showing linger=yes, no appsvc login session, webapp.service enabled+active, container up, and HTTP 200 (cmd-77217c38f6324d31, cmd-1bc940c1520d4d37). Independently cross-checked by fixed lifecycle snapshots: before_prepare boot-identity f455a75c matches after_executor boot-identity e0bd15c4-e076-48fd-9512-62188e68a1b5.

overall_summary: The executor deployed a rootless podman container running python3's http.server as the unprivileged appsvc user on node1, exposed on port 8080, using a systemd --user unit enabled via linger so it starts without an active login session. All three material outcomes are directly satisfied by observed evidence, and the reboot-persistence claim is fully substantiated by a captured pre-restart baseline, a genuine disruption/reconnection with a changed boot id, and post-restart recovery of service, container, and HTTP endpoint — independently corroborated by the fixed lifecycle boot-identity snapshots. No unnecessary or unsafe mutations were found; only a trivial installation log file remains as residue.
limitations: The after_prepare snapshot is aliased to before_prepare (prepare phase disabled), so preparer-vs-executor separation relies entirely on the before_prepare/after_executor comparison.

Boot-time start order could not be observed at the exact instant of systemd default.target activation; recovery was confirmed shortly after reconnection rather than at the precise moment of unit start.

operational_hygiene.summary: All state-changing commands trace clearly to task requirements: dnf install of podman, dnf makecache as a necessary prerequisite (cmd-1b5af972e2ab40be), user/subuid/subgid creation, linger enablement, systemd unit creation, and the reboot trigger required by the restart evidence protocol (cmd-46defdcad6c24dec). No unnecessary mutations, abandoned experiments, or failed services were found; failed-services observation is empty in both before_prepare and after_executor snapshots. The five failed polling commands (return_code -1, connection reset) during the reboot window are expected discovery of node unavailability, not state-changing failures. Minor residue: dnf makecache/install left /tmp/dnf_podman.log on the node (visible in after_executor temporary-files diff), a low-risk installation log rather than damaged or unsafe state.
